This second application has been filed by applicant under Section 438 of Code of Criminal Procedure/482 of the BNSS for grant of anticipatory bail, who is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.195/2023 registered at Police Station Gohad Chauraha, District Bhind for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 193 of IPC.
Earlier application was dismissed as withdrawn.

As per the case of prosecution offence at Crime No. 167/2022 for offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 366-A (2) (N) of IPC and 3/4 of POCSO Act was registered against Devesh Argal S/o Balkishan at P.S. Gohad Chauraha, Distt. Bhind.
Devesh Argal applied for grant of anticipatory bail.
He has submitted a photocopy of birth certificate of the victim.

The Trial Court released Devesh in compliance with the order of the High Court, however, directed the investigation officer to enquire into NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:15750 2 MCRC-39266-2024 veracity of birth certificate.
Accordingly, an enquiry was conducted with regard to veracity of the birth certificate.
CMO, Community Health Center, Bhouriya replied on query that the birth certificate was not issued by her and the concerned birth certificate is forged.
Statement of witnesses especially father and brother of the victim were also recorded.
They also verified that they have not registered birth of the victim and no birth certificate was issued.

On the findings of enquiry, FIR at Crime No. 195 of 2023 Devesh Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103470396/
1 was registered at Police Station Gohad Chauraha, Distt. Bhind for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 193 of IPC against Devesh Argal and Adarsh Argal in which investigation is underway.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application submits that applicant was granted benefit of anticipatory bail.
The anticipatory bail granted in favour of applicant has not been cancelled till date.

The birth certificate was verified on the basis of bar code on it before filing along with application for grant of anticipatory bail, however, the birth certificate was removed from the web site of department of Planning and Economics Statistics.
Applicant is not responsible for removal of the birth certificate from the concerned web site.
Applicant has bonafidely applied for bail on the basis of the birth certificate.
Applicant is ready to cooperate in the investigation and the trial.

No criminal antecedents is reported against the applicant, therefore,
applicant may be extended benefit of anticipatory bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the application.

Learned counsel referring to statement of family members of the victim NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:15750 3 MCRC-39266-2024 contends that the birth of victim was not registered for issuance of birth certificate.

Further, the issuing authority, Community Health Officer of Community Health Center,
Bhouriya, Gwalior
has specifically denied issuance of the birth certificate in question.
The applicant has not given any explanation with regard to procurement of birth certificate.
It is a case of misleading the Court to secure bail, therefore, applicant may not be extended the benefit of anticipatory bail.
Heard both the parties and perused the record.
The case diary reveals that forged birth certificate was presented to the Court, with impunity, to mislead the Court and to secure anticipatory bail.
It is not an offence against individual rather it affects the administration of criminal justice.
The bail will have large social ramification and miscreant will be encouraged to meddle with criminal justice system through illegal means.
The likelihood of committing another offence and tampering with evidence by applicant in such a scenario cannot be ruled out.
In the considered opinion of this Court, the applicant does not deserve to be released on anticipatory bail.
Consequently, the application for anticipatory bail is dismissed.

(SANJEEV S KALGAONKAR) JUDGE ar Devesh Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103470396/
